The build passes. Here's a summary of what I changed.

## Changes

The `customerCode` is generated in one place — `ClinicServiceImpl.generateCustomerCode` — and every derived value (the membership number) reads it back through `owner.getCustomerCode()`, so rebuilding the code is enough to rebuild everything built from it.

**`ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — reworked `generateCustomerCode` from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (global sequence) to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`:
- `CITY3` = upper-cased first three letters of the city
- `LAST3` = upper-cased first three letters of the last name (unchanged)
- `NNNN` = per-city 4-digit sequence, one more than the owners already in that city (city matched case-insensitively), replacing the previous global owner count

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — `formatMembershipNumber` already builds `<customerCode>-M<YY>` off `getCustomerCode()`, so it now automatically emits e.g. `SYD-SMI-0007-M26`; I only updated its Javadoc example to the new format.

The acceptance test (`coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix`, asserting `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`) and the full suite pass: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 — BUILD SUCCESS`.

One judgment call worth flagging: both the city and last-name segments are truncated to their first 3 letters with `Math.min`, matching the existing last-name handling, so a city shorter than 3 letters would yield a sub-3-char prefix (the regex expects exactly 3). The test's generated cities are always long enough, and this mirrors the pre-existing last-name behaviour, so I kept it consistent rather than adding padding the spec doesn't mention.
